title: Hierarchical Queries with Recursive CTEs (WITH RECURSIVE)
realWorldScenario: Your product catalog supports deep nested product categories (e.g., Electronics -> Audio -> Headphones -> Wireless Headphones). You need to generate the full breadcrumb path and depth level for every category.
questionStatement: Write a query using a recursive Common Table Expression (`WITH RECURSIVE`) against a hierarchical table of categories (`id`, `parent_id`, `name`) that calculates the complete ancestor path (`breadcrumb`) and hierarchical depth level for each category, ordered by path.
starterCode:
WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (
    -- Anchor member
    SELECT 
        id, 
        parent_id, 
        name,
        1 AS depth,
        name::text AS breadcrumb
    FROM categories
    WHERE parent_id IS NULL
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Recursive member
    SELECT 
        c.id, 
        c.parent_id, 
        c.name,
        ct.depth + 1,
        ct.breadcrumb || ' > ' || c.name
    FROM categories c
    JOIN category_tree ct ON c.parent_id = ct.id
)
SELECT id, name, depth, breadcrumb
FROM category_tree
ORDER BY breadcrumb;
expectedConcepts: Anchor query selecting base root records
Recursive query joining child records to working CTE table
Termination condition when recursive join returns 0 rows
Depth counting and string path accumulation
hints: Start with rows where parent_id IS NULL as the anchor.
In the recursive part, join categories to category_tree on c.parent_id = ct.id.
Increment depth by 1 and concatenate breadcrumb on each step.

testCases.description: Verify category tree breadcrumb and depth calculation
testCases.setupSql:
CREATE TABLE categories (id INT PRIMARY KEY, parent_id INT, name VARCHAR(50));
INSERT INTO categories VALUES (1, NULL, 'Electronics'), (2, 1, 'Computers'), (3, 2, 'Laptops'), (4, 1, 'Audio'), (5, 4, 'Headphones');
testCases.expectedOutputSql:
WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (
    SELECT id, parent_id, name, 1 AS depth, name::text AS breadcrumb
    FROM categories WHERE parent_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT c.id, c.parent_id, c.name, ct.depth + 1, ct.breadcrumb || ' > ' || c.name
    FROM categories c JOIN category_tree ct ON c.parent_id = ct.id
)
SELECT id, name, depth, breadcrumb FROM category_tree ORDER BY breadcrumb;
